correctness.rationale: At each p^j level, choosing a subset of 1,2,...,2^a is equivalent to an integer x_j in [0,S], S=2^(a+1)-1. Setting y_j=2x_j-S turns equal partition sums into sum y_j p^j=0 with every y_j odd and |y_j|<=S. Since p>2^a, S<2p and S+1<2p. Modulo p, y_0 must be a nonzero odd multiple of p of magnitude below 2p, so y_0=-epsilon_0 p. After division by p, p divides y_1-epsilon_0; that difference is even and has magnitude below 2p, hence it vanishes and y_1=epsilon_0. Repeating gives y_{2k}=-epsilon_k p and y_{2k+1}=epsilon_k independently for each pair. Thus there are 2^((b+1)/2) oriented partitions, and global sign reversal is exactly block swap with no fixed point, leaving 2^((b-1)/2) unordered partitions. The verifier independently enumerates bounded signed-coefficient solutions for representative upper-strip cases and a below-strip counterexample.

originality.rationale: Rao--Peng and Mahanta--Saikia--Yaqubi supply existence theory for Zumkeller numbers and the two-prime family, while a published Resultary finding gives the exact partition count only for the exponent-one family 2^a p. In the upper strip that special case equals one. No inspected source gives the all-odd-exponent multiplicity 2^((b-1)/2) or the rigid adjacent-pair sign classification. The submitted carry argument therefore extends the known b=1 count and refines the existence theorem throughout the natural upper strip.

The theorem classifies every equal-sum divisor bipartition across an infinite, structurally distinguished upper strip and extends the known exact b=1 count to all odd exponents by a rigid signed-carry mechanism.

final_claim: For a>=1, odd prime p with 2^a<p<=2^(a+1)-1, and odd b>=1, the divisors of 2^a p^b have exactly 2^((b-1)/2) unordered equal-sum complementary bipartitions.
scientific_limitations: The 2020 primary article was not materially reread in full in this run; an unadvertised counting remark remains possible.
